Our classroom starting rule: We are testing a fossil-identification method before specialist review. Of four later test specimens, we want at least three supported decisions and no wrong supported decisions. “Unresolved” means the image does not show enough evidence. This is a teaching rule for a small trial, not a professional accuracy standard. For this first walkthrough, use these settings as written. Discuss alternative rules after the exercise, not during the test. Here, a supported key decision means naming one of the three genera or ruling out all three (“Outside key”). “Unresolved” means the evidence is insufficient to do either.

Use these settings — no choices to make yet
  • Purpose: a classroom training check before specialist review.
  • Test group: four specimens.
  • Maximum wrong supported decisions: 0.
  • Minimum supported decisions: 3 out of 4.

The video uses the same numbers. We choose them before looking at reference names. A result that falls short is still useful: it tells us what the method cannot yet do.

Need help? Leave this step open and raise your hand. If GeoGPT asks a technical question, open the help below. If it asks for a missing file, attach that file; do not tell it to continue without the file. If a reply stops changing for about three minutes, ask the instructor to check it—do not repeatedly press Send.

CT means computed tomography: X-rays reveal the inside of a specimen. A projection combines many internal layers into one view; a section shows a slice through the fossil. A key is a set of visible features used to decide its name. Here we test whether Treatise anatomy supports our decisions; we are not estimating fossil abundance or geological age.

Work in English. This is a classroom training check of an anatomy-based fossil identification method before specialist review. I am learning the workflow; do not ask me to design a validation study. Use these supplied teaching defaults: four validation specimens; maximum zero wrong accepted decisions; minimum three accepted decisions out of four. An accepted decision is a supported assignment to one of our three candidate genera, or a supported Outside key decision based on incompatible visible anatomy. Unresolved means there is not enough visible evidence and does not count as accepted. Outside key does not complete a genus identification. These are teaching settings, not a professional accuracy standard, and four selected specimens cannot establish general accuracy. Record the purpose and these defaults in a short table. Explain accepted, Outside key and Unresolved in one sentence each. Do not ask me to choose a purpose, thresholds, taxonomy, software or statistical settings. Do not identify specimens or construct the key yet. Finish with: Ready for Step 2: paste the handout's Treatise anatomy prompt.

The research problem: reproducible identification from CT anatomy

Luijmes, van Leeuwen & Renema (2024), Scientific Data, released ForametCeTera to support automated fossil-image analysis. The archive contains individual reconstructed scans and author identifications. We use twelve real specimens selected by numeric ID from four scan groups; no anatomy or labels were invented.

Your narrower investigation: can a character-based protocol distinguish three Treatise genera while recognizing specimens outside that key or lacking sufficient evidence? Read the paper’s abstract and examine the specimen views. The workshop tests a protocol on selected individuals; it does not reproduce a trained classifier or a natural assemblage census.

Do this

  1. Read the three short Treatise descriptions and look at the plates below. A morphology key is a guide that links visible anatomy to a possible fossil name.
  2. Click “Copy these words” in this step. The button copies the complete instruction, the three attributed Treatise summaries, and their source links. You do not need to copy from a video or another website.
  3. Return to the same GeoGPT conversation. Paste the copied text into the message box and click Send once.
  4. Wait for a table or short set of identification rules. Check that it includes the three genera, the features to look for, and when to say Unresolved.
  5. Check its two final rules: clearly incompatible anatomy means Outside key; insufficient anatomy means Unresolved. If it reverses these, use the recovery reply below. Once the rules are correct, reply in GeoGPT: “Use this as our provisional guide for the practice specimens. Keep missing evidence as Unresolved.” Then return here and continue to Step 3.

A chamber is a compartment in the shell; a chamberlet is a smaller subdivision. A diagnostic character is a feature that helps distinguish one group from another. The key is the set of identification rules you will test.

The Treatise is the diagnostic authority for this exercise. The CT archive supplies the observations. A genus name is defensible only when the specimen shows the characters required by the key.

Treatise anatomical evidence Use these attributed summaries to construct your own key. They describe genera; they do not assign labels to the workshop specimens. The original entries are linked for checking. Alveolinella An elongated spindle-shaped test contains multiple tiers of chamberlets. Septa form a continuous arrangement; passages occur just ahead of the septa near chamber floors. Multiple aperture rows provide another character when resolved. Decide which section orientations would test the chamberlet organization. Treatise diagnosis . Marginopora A flattened, concave-sided test grows in rings of chambers. Internal partitions form chamberlets connected by passages. The central chamber system differs from the smaller lateral chamberlets. The periphery carries numerous openings. Examine the section figures below to determine what an edge-on versus equatorial view can establish. Treatise diagnosis and Fig. 385 . Original Fig. 385. Marginopora is illustrated in 3–4; 4a–b are axial sections. The other panels show related genera and are useful comparisons. This is a reference plate, not the CT dataset. Baculogypsinoides The early test follows a trochospiral arrangement; later chambers become irregularly piled. Typical specimens bear three or four stout, blunt spines. The diagnosis also describes internal vertical pillars and branching canals. Determine which of these features the scan resolves rather than assuming they are present. Treatise diagnosis and Fig. 502 . Original Fig. 502. The digitized entry identifies 1 as an equatorial section of the type species and discusses panels 2–3 under the synonym Silvestriella . Use the diagnosis and section orientation, not a species-level resemblance claim.

Treatise anatomical evidence

Use these attributed summaries to construct your own key. They describe genera; they do not assign labels to the workshop specimens. The original entries are linked for checking.

Alveolinella

An elongated spindle-shaped test contains multiple tiers of chamberlets. Septa form a continuous arrangement; passages occur just ahead of the septa near chamber floors. Multiple aperture rows provide another character when resolved. Decide which section orientations would test the chamberlet organization. Treatise diagnosis.

Marginopora

A flattened, concave-sided test grows in rings of chambers. Internal partitions form chamberlets connected by passages. The central chamber system differs from the smaller lateral chamberlets. The periphery carries numerous openings. Examine the section figures below to determine what an edge-on versus equatorial view can establish. Treatise diagnosis and Fig. 385.

Baculogypsinoides

The early test follows a trochospiral arrangement; later chambers become irregularly piled. Typical specimens bear three or four stout, blunt spines. The diagnosis also describes internal vertical pillars and branching canals. Determine which of these features the scan resolves rather than assuming they are present. Treatise diagnosis and Fig. 502.

Anatomical glossary and image limits

Chamber: a growth compartment. Chamberlet: a subdivision of a chamber. Septum: a partition between chambers. Equatorial section: a plane through the principal coiling region. Axial section: a plane containing the coiling axis. Trochospiral: coiling with displacement along an axis. Acervuline: an irregularly accumulated arrangement of chambers.

The CT data have 15 µm voxels. A feature spanning only one or two voxels is not securely characterized; interpolation cannot recover missing detail. Brightness alone does not establish a calcareous wall texture or mineral phase. An unresolved feature is not an absent feature.

Data provenance and preparation

Check the source, units and preparation choices before interpreting the results.

Actual NRRD CT specimens from ForametCeTera, doi:10.5281/zenodo.8344213, described by Luijmes et al. (2024), doi:10.1038/s41597-024-03476-w. Twelve specimens are the first three numeric IDs available in four scan groups; selection preceded image inspection. Group composition is deliberately balanced, not a natural census.

Original uint8 intensity volumes are reoriented by principal axes of nonzero voxel coordinates onto a 15 micrometre grid using linear interpolation. Maximum-intensity projections and 17 planes per axis spanning 10–90% of the aligned extent are embedded. Intensities are preserved; image scaling does not restore subvoxel information.

The development, validation and extension sets contain distinct individuals but share scan groups. Author species assignments are revealed after commitment and scored at genus/key-membership level. This is not a new species diagnosis, an independent instrument test, a trained classifier evaluation or an environmental reconstruction.

A maximum-intensity projection combines an entire voxel column. It is not a microscope photograph: overlapping structures can conceal internal architecture. The scale bar is 0.5 mm and the original voxel size is 15 µm.

Where you work: Read the instructions on this page. Send prompts, answers and files in GeoGPT. Keep both tabs open.

Do this

Open CT section viewer ↓

A chamber system can appear discontinuous in a single plane. Following it through adjacent sections tests that interpretation. Brightness does not identify mineralogy, and enlarging an image does not improve its spatial resolution.

Review development, then freeze the key

Where you work: Read the instructions on this page. Send prompts, answers and files in GeoGPT. Keep both tabs open.

Do this

  1. First verify that GeoGPT has all eight development records. Only then reveal the development reference labels below.
  2. Copy the newly available prompt. It includes the labels automatically; compare GeoGPT’s counts and critique with your own records.
  3. Approve any justified revision in GeoGPT. Ask it to freeze the final key and your original criterion before you inspect validation specimens.

Development means the first practice group, D01–D04. Freeze means keep the agreed identification rules unchanged while testing the next group. You do not need to find a Freeze button.

Development feedback can improve a protocol. It cannot be used to tune the protocol after validation labels are known. The published species labels are reference assignments, evaluated here at genus or Outside key level.

Reveal the labels and audit the scores

Where you work: Read the instructions on this page. Send prompts, answers and files in GeoGPT. Keep both tabs open.

Do this

  1. Check that all eight validation decisions are visible in GeoGPT. Then reveal the validation labels below and copy the resulting prompt.
  2. Check one reported numerator and denominator yourself. Count wrong accepted decisions, Outside key referrals and unresolved cases separately.
  3. Compare the actual counts with your original criterion. Accepting Outside key is a decision about this key, not a completed genus identification.

In a fraction, the numerator is the number being counted, and the denominator is the total group being compared. Ask GeoGPT to say exactly which specimens it counted in each.

Coverage and accuracy answer different questions. Abstaining can reduce accepted errors while increasing specialist-review burden. Four specimens cannot establish population performance.
